solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New TV channel backing a state

indicators.note: backing here means the channel's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Dave is a UK television channel

explanation.surface: A new television channel is putting its support behind one of the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave is a British TV channel. 'backing' looks like sponsorship but is the signal to read it from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Start to pay attention when going above US marshal

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going above another is placed before it

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention, so ear means attention

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to begin listening carefully when you outrank a US marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'going above' puts EAR on top of the P from 'pay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a famous lawman of the Old West who served as a deputy US marshal.

clue.text: Stands by statute I'd amended

indicators.note: a statute that is amended is changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes positions supported by a statute that they have amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' rearranges STATUTE plus ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand on an issue is a position or opinion, a synonym of attitude.

clue.text: Remove tip of thin, small projectiles

indicators.note: removing the tip of a word takes away its first letter

parts.note: narrow means thin

explanation.surface: An instruction to blunt slender, small missiles by taking off their points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove tip of' takes the N off NARROW to leave ARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrows are shot from bows, so they are a kind of missile or projectile.

clue.text: The lady's not for turning, as posited

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against, the opposite of for

indicators.note: turning here means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to posit it, so set means posited

explanation.surface: An echo of Thatcher's famous line that the lady was not for turning, as was claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses AS SET to give TESSA. The surface quotes Margaret Thatcher's 1980 speech, 'The lady's not for turning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a titled noblewoman, so she is a lady.

clue.text: Meat product that's cold, as far I can see? Not quite

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: the horizon is the limit of how far one can see

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a cold cut and wonders if it is really meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of HORIZON.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage, a manufactured meat product.

clue.text: Notice about holding in toxin

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other
about can mean around or astir, so these letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A posted notice warns that some poison is being kept inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals a rearrangement, and 'holding' places the second piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the poisonous alkaloid in tobacco, so it is a toxin.

clue.text: Jostle group

definitions.meaning: to push or shove one's way through
A British rock band, a musical group

explanation.surface: A crowd pushing and shoving.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbowing is jostling with the arms, and Elbow is the name of an English band.

clue.text: Old herbivores mostly used to grass being sown

indicators.note: seed being sown is scattered about, so these letters are scattered into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ancient plant-eaters largely accustomed to grass seed being planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts USED to USE; 'being sown' rearranges USE, TO and GRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stegosaurs were plant-eating dinosaurs of the Jurassic period, ancient herbivores.

clue.text: Composition of old men put in proportion

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a ratio is a proportion
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the make-up of veterans fitted into the right proportion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other ranks' is the British army term for soldiers who are not officers, hence men.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra, a composition.

clue.text: Snare company partners entering the books

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: B is book, so books doubled gives BB
West and East are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A business snares partners who are joining its accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, players sit as partnerships North-South and East-West, so W and E are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a trap for insects, so a cobweb is a kind of snare.

clue.text: He that's after a little bit in a very short skirt, finding love — such a hoot

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the earlier one
in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tutu is the very short skirt worn by ballerinas
a whit is a tiny amount
who means he that, as in 'who dares wins'
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man chasing a woman in a miniskirt and falling for her: what a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoot' reads as a laugh in the surface but means an owl's call here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tu-whit tu-whoo is the conventional rendering of an owl's call, which is a hoot.

clue.text: Pressure to involve half-taught vamp

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap something up inside

parts.note: stress means pressure

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: educated means taught

explanation.surface: Applying pressure to involve a partly trained flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first four letters of a synonym of 'taught', not of the printed word, and 'to involve' places them after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a woman who uses her charms to seduce men, a femme fatale.

clue.text: Old hat, stovepipe, finally packed away by old man

indicators.note: packed away by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: old man is slang for father, a dad

indicators.note: finally picks out the very last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned stovepipe hat that father finally stored away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like the stovepipe itself but means out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat means outdated or no longer interesting, as is something dead.

clue.text: Drink in endless bout, certain to get dizzy

indicators.note: something made dizzy is spun round, so these letters are mixed up
endless means the word loses both its end letters

explanation.surface: A drinker in an unending bout is sure to end up dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips BOUT to OU, and 'to get dizzy' rearranges OU with CERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is an orange-flavoured French liqueur, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Nothing will stop new research — you can bet on it

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so this piece goes inside
new means the word is made afresh, its letters rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A confident claim that fresh research will never be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RESEARCH to RACEHRSE, and 'will stop' puts O into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters place wagers on a horse in a race, so it is something to bet on.

clue.text: Attempt every year to get most of tip for foreign food

parts.note: to have a pop at something is to attempt it
PA, per annum, means each year

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

explanation.surface: Trying yearly to get most out of a rubbish site in search of exotic food.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is British for a rubbish dump; 'most of' cuts DUMP to DUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A poppadum is a thin, crisp Indian flatbread, a food from abroad.

clue.text: Free part of wheel, stuck in remote north

indicators.note: stuck in means one piece is jammed inside the other

parts.note: remote, as in an out-of-the-way place, means out
a spoke is one of the rods of a wheel

explanation.surface: A loose bit of a wheel stuck somewhere in the remote north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like loose but means frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspoken speech is free and frank, saying what one thinks.

clue.text: Times chief points the wrong way for humanist

parts.note: eras are times or periods

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the sum of a matter is its main points, its gist

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor makes an error of direction while hunting a humanist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' and 'chief' suggest the newspaper's editor; 'the wrong way' reverses SUM to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance scholar of humanism.

clue.text: Chinese restaurant emptied? Sure thing

indicators.note: a word emptied loses all its middle letters, leaving only the outside two

explanation.surface: A Chinese restaurant with no customers is a certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Cert is British slang, short for certainty, for a sure thing such as a racing favourite.

clue.text: Free time to drop in snooker accessories

indicators.note: to drop means the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a rest is the stick used to support a snooker cue for long shots
a cue is the stick used to strike the ball in snooker

explanation.surface: Free time to call in on the snooker gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a British billiards game; a rest and a cue are its equipment. 'to drop' takes the T out of REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from danger is to rescue them, so the two verbs mean the same.

clue.text: State hated us anyhow for holding back Republican idiot

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps around the other
anyhow means in any old order, so these letters are rearranged
back means this run is read backwards

parts.note: prat is British slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: A state hated the US for detaining an idiotic Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges HATED US into UT...ADESH, which holds TARPR, the R and PRAT reversed by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttar Pradesh is India's most populous state, in the north of the country.

clue.text: Foreign area upset male

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Neil is a man's name, standing for a male

explanation.surface: A man is upset about a foreign area.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'upset' turns NEIL up to give LIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means belonging to another country or people, strange.

clue.text: Bargain method of family planning?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a bargain, something cheap
slang for a vasectomy, a means of contraception

explanation.surface: A cheap way to plan a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is something sold cheaply, and the snip is colloquial for a vasectomy.

clue.text: Stern minimalist order from stag to his mate?

parts.note: be is the shortest possible command, a single verb
a hind is a female deer, mate of the stag

explanation.surface: A stag gives his partner the barest of commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' means the back, as of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear of a ship, the part that is at the back.

clue.text: Dandy once caught in Romania after revolution

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
after a revolution the order is overturned, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A former fop is arrested in Romania after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' signals a rearrangement of the country's name, which then takes the cricket C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In 18th-century Britain a macaroni was a fashionable young man who aped continental styles.

clue.text: Star interrupting cheers by girl, briefly causing waves

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
the sun is a star

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: miss means a girl

explanation.surface: A celebrity breaks up applause for a girl, briefly making a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing waves' looks like the definition, but only 'waves' is; 'cheers' is British for thanks, TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave set off by an earthquake, so tsunamis are waves.

clue.text: Former member entering extremely expedient excuse

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other piece
extremely picks out the two extreme letters of the word

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a member

explanation.surface: An ex-politician offers a very convenient excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excuse' is a verb here: to let off.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a duty is to exempt them, release them from it.
